$comment: Size ceilings (bytes) for the SHIPPED studio build, checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts in test.yml's gated `studio-dist` job, after a real `bun run build`. Studio is a dev tool so end users do not download it, but it is otherwise unmonitored (the codecov bundle path is broken — see codecov-bundle-analysis-diagnosis.md). Raise a ceiling deliberately, with justification, when a real feature grows it. A directory key budgets its whole tree minus source maps.
$ratchet: monaco-editor 0.55.1 -> 0.56.0 moved the metafile build 14202972 -> 14572625 bytes (+369653, +2.6%), and the split release build 13822091 -> 14189667 over the same change. The old 14000000 ceiling was already being met on tolerance rather than under the ceiling (main sat at 101.4%), which is how a real 2.6% growth would have been absorbed silently. Raised deliberately to just above the measured figure so the next regression has to be argued for.
$ratchet-kit-coexistence: The UI kit joined the startup path (registerKit(): its component documents, the Phosphor manifest for the ~100 glyphs the shell uses, and the theme sheet) while Spectrum stays registered until the last lit surface migrates, moving studio.js 2931123 -> 3032009 (+100886, +3.4%), on tolerance against the 3000000 ceiling. Raised to just above the measured figure for the coexistence period; it comes back DOWN in the removal PR, when the 36 Spectrum packages leave. The keyed-list reconciler and mount() in the runtime moved iframe-entry.js 266632 -> 278364 (+11732, +4.4%) on the same rule.
$was-measuring-the-wrong-thing: Until now the only budgeted key was studio.js at 14600000, and it was checked on the bundle-analysis lane after `bun run build:metafile` — a single unsplit `bun build` with no splitting and no shared contract, which inlines Monaco and everything else. That lane wrote its output to dist/ too, so it OVERWROTE the release build's studio.js at the same path. The artifact that actually ships is 2.93 MB, five times smaller, and had no ceiling at all; neither did iframe-entry.js, chunks/ or workers/. The metafile lane writes to dist-metafile/ now and the budgets below are measured from `bun run build`.
$ratchet-iframe-entry: Change highlighting (git-diff artboards) added DIFF_MARK_CSS, syncDiffCss and applyDiffMarks to iframe-render.ts, moving iframe-entry.js 257959 -> 260075 bytes (+2116, +0.8%). The old 260000 ceiling was then being met on TOLERANCE rather than under the ceiling (100.0%), which is the exact shape the studio.js note below warns about: the next real growth would be absorbed silently. Raised to just above the measured figure so it has to be argued for instead. Then browser verification split a modification into the two faces it wears (red on the committed side, green on the working copy — marked identically it read as 'added' over the very text being replaced), which is one more CSS rule: 260075 -> 266632, and 101.8% of the 262000 set above. Raised again to just above the measured figure, on the same rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-iframe-entry-dialogs: Dialogs shown in place (studio.md §4.2.3) added the dialog rules, applyCanvasDialogOpen, the setDialogOpen and redefineElement handlers and the commandTargetClick report to the frame, moving iframe-entry.js 279541 -> 284792 bytes (+5251, +1.9%) — over the 280000 ceiling and onto the tolerance, which is the shape every note in this file warns about. Raised to just above the measured figure, on the same rule.
$ratchet-spectrum-removal: The $ratchet-kit-coexistence note above promised this and it came due: the 36 @spectrum-web-components entries (50 resolved, plus colorjs.io, @lit-labs/virtualizer and lit itself, which nothing imported once the two LitElement selectors went) left packages/studio, and with them the registry, the brand fragment and styles/spectrum.css. studio.js 4140570 -> 2640946 bytes (-1499624, -36.2%), so the 3040000 ceiling comes back DOWN to 2700000 — just above the measured figure, on this file's own rule, and below both figures the coexistence note cites (3032009 during coexistence, 2931123 before the kit). That prediction was right about the direction and wrong about the size, in the honest direction: it expected a return to roughly the pre-kit 2.93 MB, and the shipped bundle is 290177 bytes UNDER that, because the kit weighs less than the lit templates and Spectrum classes it replaced. chunks goes 12500000 -> 12900000, and that RAISE is the one number here that grows. It is justified rather than convenient: the measured figure is 12752619, which is over the old ceiling and reaches green only through the 5% tolerance — the shape every note in this file warns about — and the ceiling was already unmet before this change, because Spectrum was only about 590 KB of that tree. iframe-entry.js 290788 -> 289726 and workers 13617430 -> 13617430, byte-identical, which is what says the before and after are measurements of the same tree.
$measure-with-no-dev-server-running: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING A NUMBER FROM THIS FILE. `scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts` measures whatever is in `dist/`, and `bun run build` wipes that directory first — so the figures above are clean by construction, but only if nothing else is writing there. A `bun run dev` watcher is: it rebuilds the studio bundle on save, into the same `dist/`, AFTER the wipe and without one of its own, so its output accumulates beside the release build's under different chunk hashes. Measured on the Spectrum-removal branch: with a dev server up, chunks reported 25498884 bytes and the gate failed at 197.7%; the very next `bun run build` with the server stopped reported 12752619 across 107 chunks, with ZERO byte-identical duplicates under a hash- and debugId-normalising comparison. Same commit, same command, twice the bytes. That is worth writing down because it has already misled once: the §C8 survey measured 25977090 across 267 files and attributed 8922445 of it to the two-pass build emitting shared chunks twice, including two Monaco chunks of 5086021 and 5082169 differing in four lines — which is exactly the shape a stale watcher leaves behind, and which one clean rebuild does not reproduce. Treat the duplicate-chunk finding as unproven rather than as fixed by anything in this change: nothing here touched the build's splitting.
$ratchet-iframe-entry-c8: C8 moved iframe-entry.js DOWN, 290788 -> 289726 bytes, and it is still 101.3% of the 286000 ceiling — green only on TOLERANCE, which is the exact shape every note above warns about: the next real growth would be absorbed silently. C8 did not cause the overrun (the canvas realm gained the keyed reconciler, mount() and the dialog transposition across A1/A2/A5) and it is not this slice's to explain, but leaving a key on tolerance because the number improved is how a budget stops budgeting. Raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's own standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-kit-loaders: The canvas frame registers the kit's behaviour sidecars as LAZY loaders (embedding.md §6, ui.md §10): a project on the canvas that uses a kit element names its sidecar by `jx-ui:` specifier, which nothing served, so every kit element with a behaviour failed to mount there (measured on stylebook/jx-combobox.json: ten elements, none reaching its control). The fix is a table of twenty-two `import()` thunks in iframe-entry.ts, one chunk per module on first use, so a page that draws no kit element loads none of them. Measured on a clean `bun run build` with the watcher stopped: iframe-entry.js 290146 -> 292918 (+2772, +1.0%, the table and the preloadModule import) and chunks 12860026 -> 13004222 (+144196, +1.1%: twenty-two behaviour chunks, the largest icons at 47615 because it carries the glyph manifest, and the shared pieces the splitter lifted out of studio.js, which moved 2649372 -> 2652418). Both keys were on tolerance afterwards (100.3% and 100.8%), which is the shape every note in this file warns about, so both are raised to just above the measured figure on the file's own standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance. The eager alternative — seeding all twenty into the entry — was measured at 46024 bytes minified before this was chosen, and rejected because the frame renders whatever project is open and most projects draw no kit element at all.
